title: Non-Abelian Spin Counting of Ordered Stochastic Trajectories: Reentrant Finite-Time Chern Numbers
abstract: Conventional full counting statistics assigns commuting phases to integrated stochastic currents and therefore resolves net transport but not, in general, the temporal ordering of events associated with different cycles. We introduce a non-Abelian counting construction in which crossings of two fundamental cycles rotate an auxiliary spin about different axes. The resulting ordered trajectory statistic has an exact finite-dimensional evolution equation for its first moment. The two rotation angles form a counting torus, and whenever the mean spin is nonzero its normalized direction defines a map $\mathbb T^2\to\mathbb S^2$, equivalently a complex eigenline bundle with a Chern number. Our main analytical result is a Chern--parity correspondence. Reflection symmetry equips this eigenline with a real structure and expresses $C_T\bmod2$ through first Stiefel--Whitney classes on the circles fixed by reflection. When the transverse polarization has no additional zeros along the reflection-fixed circles, these classes reduce to ordinary current-parity statistics at the four high-symmetry counting points. For a five-state nonequilibrium figure-eight network, varying only the observation time produces four polarization-gap closings and the reentrant sequence $C_T=0\to-1\to0\to-1\to0$. Every transition occurs at $(π,π)$ and coincides with a sign reversal of $\mathbb E[(-1)^{Q_1+Q_2}]$, while the full integer Chern number is obtained independently from the two-dimensional spin texture. Finite observation time can therefore organize a fixed stochastic process into distinct topological sectors of its ordered path ensemble.
summary: This paper develops a non-Abelian counting statistic to track the temporal ordering of events in stochastic processes, moving beyond the limitations of standard Full Counting Statistics. By mapping the ordered path ensemble to a complex line bundle, the authors calculate a Chern number ($C_T$) that quantifies this ordering. This shows that finite observation time can force a fixed process into distinct, topologically characterized sectors.
main_problem: To develop a counting statistic that captures the temporal ordering of stochastic events associated with different cycles, overcoming the limitation of conventional Full Counting Statistics (FCS) which only resolves net transport.
main_result: The non-Abelian counting construction yields a Chern number ($C_T$) that is sensitive to the temporal ordering of paths, demonstrating a Chern–parity correspondence with ordinary current-parity statistics.
method: The authors introduce a non-Abelian counting construction using noncommuting rotations of an auxiliary spin, mapping the problem to calculating the Chern number of a complex line bundle over the counting torus.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on a five-state nonequilibrium figure-eight network, modeled as a stochastic Markov process with oriented cycles A and B.
key_observables: The Chern number ($C_T$), the mean spin $\mathbf{m}_T(\alpha, 	heta)$, and the parity observable $	ext{E}[(-1)^{Q_1+Q_2}]$ are key diagnostics.
important_parameters: Observation time $T$, and the parameters defining the cycle affinities ($A_i$).
main_assumptions: The underlying dynamics are assumed to be classical and Markovian; the analysis relies on the existence of reflection symmetry to simplify the topological invariant calculation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the two-loop Markov network and the associated counting gauge, showing spin rotations on specific edges. The notes detail the reentrant sequence of $C_T$ when varying observation time.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the failure of Abelian FCS to introducing the non-Abelian spin counting, deriving the topological invariant (Chern number), establishing the Chern–parity correspondence, and finally applying this to show time-dependent topological sectors in the path ensemble.
why_interesting: The connection between non-equilibrium stochastic processes, topological invariants (Chern numbers), and path ordering is highly relevant for understanding fluctuation theorems and non-equilibrium steady states in complex quantum or classical systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Two-loop Markov network and the counting gauge. On cycle A the forward orientation 0 →1 →2 →0 has rate k1,+ and the reverse orientation has rate k1,−; cycle B is defined analogously. The auxiliary spin rotates only on the two distinguished closing edges, with inverse rotations on reverse jumps. The counter is passive and does not modify the transition rates.

Figure 2: Normalized mean-spin texture at T = 4. The component plots display the parameter-space structure, while the coordinate-net plot shows how the counting torus folds over the target sphere. The strong deformation near (π, π) is associated with the small polarization norm there.

Figure 3: Finite-time topological phase scan and parity signature. (a) Joint-current parity observable ZT (π, π) = Peven −Podd on a symmetric logarithmic scale; dotted lines mark its four zero crossings. (b) The four high-symmetry polarizations. The first three remain positive, while ZT (π, π) changes sign four times. (c) Polarization gap ∆pol(T), which closes at the same four critical times. (d) Chern number obtained independently from spherical triangulation. At each critical time the eigenline bundle is undefined because the mean polarization vanishes.
